ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices A, B, C of the rhombus OABC are on the circle $\odot O$. A tangent to $\odot O$ passing through point B intersects the extension of OA at point D. If the radius of $\odot O$ is 1, what is the length of BD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Draw line OB, then OB=OA=1, since BD is the tangent of circle O, thus $\angle$OBD=90$^\circ$, since quadrilateral OABC is a rhombus, thus OA=OB, therefore $\triangle$OAB is an equilateral triangle, hence $\angle$AOB=60$^\circ$, therefore $\angle$ADB=30$^\circ$, hence OD=2OB=2, therefore BD=$ \sqrt{OA^{2}-OB^{2}}$=$ \boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices A, B, C of the rhombus OABC are on the circle \(\odot O\). A tangent to \(\odot O\) passing through point B intersects the extension of OA at point D. If the radius of \(\odot O\) is 1, what is the length of BD?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Draw line OB. Then OB = OA = 1. Since BD is tangent to circle O, \(\angle OBD = 90^\circ\). Since quadrilateral OABC is a rhombus, OA = OB. Therefore \(\triangle OAB\) is equilateral, hence \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\). Therefore \(\angle ADB = 30^\circ\), hence OD = 2OB = 2. Therefore \(BD = \sqrt{OA^2 - OB^2} = \boxed{\sqrt{3}}\).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a circle with center O, and O is located in the upper part inside the circle; A is on the lower-left side of the circle, B is below the circle, and C is on the lower-right side of the circle. The line segments OA, AB, BC, CO form the rhombus OABC. The horizontal straight line through B is the tangent line to the circle, and to the left it intersects the extension line of OA at D; therefore D, A, O are on the same straight line, and D, B are on the tangent line. Reasoning: Connect OB. Because A, B, C are all on the circle with center O, and the radius is 1, OA = OB = 1. Also because OABC is a rhombus, AB = OA = 1. Thus the three sides OA, OB, AB of triangle OAB are all equal to 1, therefore triangle OAB is an equilateral triangle, ∠AOB = 60°. Since D is on the extension line of OA, ∠BOD = 60°. Also because BD is the tangent line to the circle at point B, the radius OB is perpendicular to the tangent line BD, so ∠OBD = 90°. Therefore triangle OBD is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, in which OB = 1 is the short leg, and the hypotenuse OD = 2. By the Pythagorean theorem, BD = sqrt(OD^2 - OB^2) = sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3).
